title: SDK extension pack authoring guidelines and sample templates
author: Priya Rao
content:
Overview

This document defines the standards, templates, and sample artifacts for authoring SDK extension packs (a.k.a. plugins, adapters, extension-packs) that integrate with Redwood SDKs. Extension packs are distributable bundles that add functionality (connectors, tokenizers, sampling strategies, prompts bundles, or telemetry hooks) while preserving the core SDK contract.

Goals
- Provide a minimal, reproducible packaging format for extension packs that is easy to review and test.
- Reduce regressions and support load from third-party or internal extensions by enforcing compatibility checks and CI gates.
- Offer ready-to-use templates and examples to speed developer onboarding.

When to use an extension pack
1. You need to add protocol-level translation (e.g., a third-party embedding service adapter).
2. You want to share reusable prompt templates and prompt-eval suites across teams.
3. You need local instrumentation that augments Redwood telemetry for a specific product integration.
4. For experimentation: new sampling strategies, rerankers or a custom cache layer.

Non-goals
- This is not a spec for modifying the Redwood runtime or core SDK internals. For that see the runtime contribution ADR.
- Not intended to authorize unrestricted network access; network permissions must be declared in the manifest and pass security review.

Core concepts and constraints
- Contract-first: extension packs must adhere to the official SDK contract (APIs, initialization lifecycle, and error surface). Reference: sdk-contract-v1.1 (link internal).
- Semantic versioning: each extension pack uses semver for its own releases and declares its compatible SDK ranges (e.g., "redwood-sdk": ">=2.3.0 <3.0.0").
- Manifest-driven packaging: a single manifest file (extension.json) describes metadata, capabilities, dependencies, and required permissions.
- Lint and testable: every pack must include a lint config and unit tests that run in the canonical CI image.
- Telemetry opt-in/out: telemetry hooks must default to opt-out and respect tenant-level telemetry settings.

Minimum manifest (extension.json)
- name: short machine-friendly id (kebab-case)
- display_name: human-friendly name
- version: semver
- author: person or team
- description: one-line summary
- sdk_compatibility: semver range for Redwood SDKs
- capabilities: list (e.g., "embedder", "prompt-bundle", "telemetry-hook", "cli")
- entrypoint: path to module exposing the init API
- permissions: list of declared runtime permissions (network, filesystem)
- license: SPDX identifier

Sample extension.json
{
  "name": "example-embedder",
  "display_name": "Example Embedder Adapter",
  "version": "0.3.0",
  "author": "search-team",
  "description": "Adapter to route embeddings to ExampleCorp service",
  "sdk_compatibility": ">=2.4.0 <3.0.0",
  "capabilities": ["embedder", "telemetry-hook"],
  "entrypoint": "lib/index.js",
  "permissions": ["network:examplecorp.com"],
  "license": "Apache-2.0"
}

Authoring guidelines
- API surface: Provide a single exported factory function (initExtension) with signature: function initExtension({ sdk, logger, config }) -> { hooks?: {}, commands?: {}, adapters?: {} }
- Idempotent init: extensions must be safe to initialize multiple times in a process.
- Non-blocking startup: heavy initialization (model warmup, file downloads) should be done asynchronously and surface progress via promises/events.
- Fail-open policy: if an extension fails to initialize at runtime, it must return a descriptive error and the SDK should fall back to core behavior unless the extension declares a fatal capability.
- Configuration: accept a typed config schema (JSON Schema v7) and a defaults.json file. Validate config at startup and failfast in CI.
- Secrets: do not embed secrets in the package. Support KMS/HSM-backed secret resolution and document required envs.

Testing and CI requirements
- Unit tests: 100% coverage is not required, but key code paths must be covered (init, error handling, and network failure simulation).
- Integration test: Each pack must include an integration test that runs against the Redwood SDK integration harness (docker image: redwood/sdk-integ:stable). The test must validate: init, a canonical request/response cycle, and graceful degradation when the adapter endpoint returns 5xx.
- Linting: Pass the extension-lint profile (eslint + typescript ruleset).
- Security scan: Run the dependency-scan and container-scan stage; no critical-high CVEs in dependencies.
- CI gate: a PR cannot be merged until all tests, lint, and security stages pass.

Template catalog (pack skeletons)
- minimal-node-extension: Node.js extension with manifest, init shim, unit test, and CI workflow.
- python-embedder: Python adapter packaging with poetry + wheel artifacts and SDK binding example.
- prompt-bundle-starter: YAML/JSON prompt group format, eval harness and golden tests.
- telemetry-hook-template: safe telemetry extension that implements opt-out and sample-rate controls.

Packaging and distribution
- Artifact: an extension pack is published as a single artifact with the following files at top level: extension.json, README.md, LICENSE, dist/ (bundled code), tests/ (integration harness).
- Registry: internal extension registry (ext-registry.redwood.internal) is the default distribution path. Public distribution requires security and legal signoff.
- Signing: all published packs must be signed using the org artifact signing key; CI will attach a .sig file.

Compatibility and migration checklist
- Declare sdk_compatibility in manifest.
- Add unit test that runs against the oldest compatible SDK version (matrix).
- Add migration notes in CHANGELOG.md describing required config changes and behavioral diffs.
- Use feature-detection where possible instead of hard SDK-version checks.

Operational runbook (support and playbook)
1. On support ticket: ask for the pack name, version, SDK version, and a reproducible snippet.
2. Reproduce using the canonical integ image: docker run -it --rm -v $(pwd):/workspace redwood/sdk-integ:stable /bin/bash; run the pack's integ tests.
3. Telemetry: check extension-specific telemetry channel (ext.<pack-name>.errors) and sample traces using Trace ID in the request.
4. Common fixes: mismatch in sdk_compatibility (update manifest), missing permissions (declare network host), initialization timeout (increase async init timeout in config).

Canonical fixes and patterns for top issues
- Installation failures (missing peer deps): document peerDependencies and include an install script to verify environment.
- Initialization race: prefer async init API and surface progress events; add retry/backoff in network calls.
- Metric leakage: ensure extension registers metrics with the SDK metrics namespace and uses proper labels; add an unregister() to cleanup on unload.
- Telemetry over-collection: provide sample_rate config and respect tenant opt-out flags.

Example: minimal Node extension (lib/index.js)
// lib/index.js (example snippet)
module.exports.initExtension = async function initExtension({ sdk, logger, config }) {
  if (!config.endpoint) throw new Error('endpoint required');
  const client = createClient(config.endpoint);
  return {
    adapters: {
      embedder: async (input) => {
        try {
          const res = await client.embed(input.text);
          return res.vectors;
        } catch (err) {
          logger.error('embedder failed', { err });
          throw err;
        }
      }
    },
    teardown: async () => { await client.close(); }
  }
}

Publishing checklist
- Bump semver and update extension.json.
- Run full CI and publish to the internal registry.
- Attach CHANGELOG.md and migration notes to the release.
- Notify SDK release channel if this pack adds or modifies public capabilities.

Security and compliance notes
- Network permissions must be minimal and declared in manifest; any broad permission ("network:*") requires security review.
- If the pack processes customer data, it must document data flows and retention in PRIVACY.md and pass the data-residency checklist.
- For private deployments, ensure the pack supports VPC endpoints and does not rely on public DNS-only endpoints.

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: author team listed in manifest.
- On-call: extension packs should list an on-call rotation in the README (team contact, pager channel).
- Escalation path: SDK support -> SDK core oncall -> Security SIG (for vulnerability or data incidents).

Appendix: quick CLI for pack validation
# validate extension pack
redwood-ext-cli validate --manifest extension.json --bundle dist/
# run integration tests locally
redwood-ext-cli integ --image redwood/sdk-integ:stable --manifest extension.json

Appendix: example release workflow (gitlab-ci snippet)
stages:
  - lint
  - test
  - security-scan
  - publish

lint_job:
  stage: lint
  script: |
    npm ci
    npm run lint
  only: [merge_requests]

publish_job:
  stage: publish
  script: |
    ./scripts/bundle.sh
    ./scripts/sign-artifact.sh dist/pack.tgz
    curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $EXT_REGISTRY_TOKEN\" -F \"file=@dist/pack.tgz\" https://ext-registry.redwood.internal/api/v1/upload
  only: [tags]

Contacts and resources
- SDK extension policy: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/policies/sdk-extension-policy (internal)
- Extension test harness image: redwood/sdk-integ:stable
- CLI: redwood-ext-cli (repo: internal/ext-cli)
- For questions: slack #sdk-extensions, or ping Priya Rao
